steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Corporate social responsibility (CSR) means businesses consider their impact on society and the environment, not just profit. | Key Fact: Ethical issues include: fair pay and working conditions, avoiding sweatshops, honest advertising, paying fair taxes, and sourcing materials responsibly. | Key Fact: Environmental considerations include: reducing carbon footprint, recycling, sustainable sourcing, minimising waste, and complying with environmental laws. | Key Fact: Pressure groups can influence business behaviour through campaigns, boycotts, and negative publicity - e.g. Greenpeace targeting companies with poor environmental records.

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Explain what is meant by corporate social responsibility and give two examples of how a business might demonstrate it. | Analyse how pressure groups can influence a business's decisions. | Evaluate whether a clothing retailer should switch to using only fair trade cotton, even though it will increase costs by 15%.
